`data-manifest.csv` (repo root) — the only CSV that holds the co-detection set.

It lists all 11 CHIME/DSA co-detected FRBs, each as two rows (`chime` + `dsa`), with columns: `burst,telescope,dm_pc_cm3,filename,arc_path,sha256,bytes,status`. Sources: casey, chromatica, freya, hamilton, isha, johndoeII, mahi, oran, phineas, whitney, wilhelm, zach.

Caveat: `CLAUDE.md` also names `chimedsa_burst_specs.csv` (the nickname↔TNS mapping) — that file does **not** exist anywhere in the tree, and nothing in the code references it. The burst registry that actually exists is `configs/bursts.yaml` (YAML, not CSV), plus `codetections_manifest.yaml`. So if you specifically wanted nickname→TNS names, that CSV isn't present; `data-manifest.csv` is the real co-detection CSV.

Want me to fix the stale `chimedsa_burst_specs.csv` reference in CLAUDE.md?

You're right — it's **12**, not 11. My earlier count was wrong; `data-manifest.csv` actually has all 12 (I miscounted casey…zach). The spreadsheet confirms 12 co-detected FRBs and gives the nickname↔TNS map that the phantom `chimedsa_burst_specs.csv` was supposed to hold:

| nickname | TNS | MJD | z_spec |
|---|---|---|---|
| zach | FRB 20220207C | 59617.809 | 0.043 |
| whitney | FRB 20220310F | 59648.242 | 0.479 |
| oran | FRB 20220506D | 59705.597 | 0.3005 |
| isha | FRB 20221113A | 59896.387 | 0.2505 |
| wilhelm | FRB 20221203A | 59916.002 | 0.510 |
| phineas | FRB 20230307A | 60010.379 | 0.271 |
| freya | FRB 20230325A | 60028.072 | — |
| johndoeII | FRB 20230814B | 60369.371 | — |
| hamilton | FRB 20230913A | 60170.361 | 0.3024 |
| mahi | FRB 20240119A | 60200.207 | — |
| chromatica | FRB 20240203A | 60331.104 | 0.074 |
| casey | FRB 20240229A | 60343.832 | 0.287 |

(freya, johndoeII, mahi have no spectroscopic z.)

**What the 3 sheets are** — same dataset, three layouts:

- **Sheet1** (96×14, "stacked/long") — top block = the 12-burst property table; below it, per-burst foreground tables stacked vertically: **Intervening Halos** (`IGH`: obj_ID, Survey, impact_kpc, RA/Dec, z_phot, class, prob_gal/star/qso) and **Intervening Clusters** (`IGC`: obj_name, Survey, impact, RA/Dec, z_phot, r500, lam500, M500, Ngal). Headers repeat and shift columns per burst — the messiest sheet.
- **Sheet2** (38×34, "wide/relational") — cleanest. Each burst row leads (cols 0–11: name…tau), then a halo block (cols 12–22, label A,B,C…) and a cluster block (cols 23–33, label I,II,III…) to the right; foreground continuation rows have the burst columns blank.
- **Sheet3** (13×6, "minimal") — just TNS, MJD, Localization, RA_deg, Dec_deg, z_spec for the 12.

Burst-level columns (Sheet1/2): `name, TNS, MJD, Localization, RA_deg, Dec_deg, z_spectroscopic, gamma_1.4GHz_MHz (+err, +NE2001), tau_1GHz_ms (+std)`.

Foreground counts per burst (from Sheet2): zach 1 halo/1 cluster · whitney 4/3 · oran 1/0 · isha 0/0 · wilhelm 1/0 · phineas 11/8 · freya 2/0 · johndoeII 0/0 · hamilton 2/0 · mahi 0/0 · chromatica 3/0 · casey 9/4.

Disorganization to handle on ingest: duplicate cols in Sheet1 (`Localization`/`z_spectroscopic` appear twice), `z_spec` written as `-` vs `NaN` vs full precision, scientific-notation leaks (a Dec rendered `7.17E+01`; some prob values too), `Impact_Parmeter_kpc` typo, and per-burst sub-headers that vary (`prob_gal/star/qso` vs `p_gal` vs `class`-only).

Sheets are mutually consistent (Sheet2 = relational merge of Sheet1; Sheet3 = burst subset). Recommended next step: normalize into two tidy CSVs — `bursts.csv` (12 rows, one per FRB) + `foreground.csv` (one row per intervening halo/cluster, keyed by nickname/TNS, `type ∈ {halo,cluster}`) — from Sheet2 as the authoritative source. Want me to build those, and where should they land (`configs/`? repo root next to `data-manifest.csv`)?

Building the normalizer now. Sheet1 attributes that cluster correctly to whitney. So I'm building foreground from **Sheet1** (explicit per-burst section headers = trustworthy attribution) and using Sheet2 only as a cross-check.

144	        zh = row.host_z_spec
145	        if np.isfinite(zh) and zh > 0:
146	            da = Planck18.angular_diameter_distance(zh)
147	            imp_zhost = (sep.radian * da).to(u.kpc).value
148	    if np.isfinite(row.impact_kpc_listed) and np.isfinite(imp_zphot) and imp_zphot > 0:
149	        ratio = imp_zphot / row.impact_kpc_listed
150	        if not (0.8 < ratio < 1.25):
151	            flags.append("IMPACT_MISMATCH_zphot")
152	    zh = row.host_z_spec
153	    if not np.isfinite(zh):
154	        flags.append("HOST_Z_UNKNOWN")
155	    elif np.isfinite(row.z_phot) and row.z_phot >= zh:
156	        flags.append("NOT_FOREGROUND_zphot>=zhost")
157	    return pd.Series(
158	        dict(
159	            sep_arcsec=sep_as,
160	            impact_kpc_recomp_zphot=imp_zphot,
161	            impact_kpc_recomp_zhost=imp_zhost,
162	            impact_ratio_zphot=ratio,
163	            flags="|".join(flags),
164	        )
165	    )
166	
167	
168	vdf = fdf.apply(verify, axis=1)
169	fdf = pd.concat([fdf, vdf], axis=1)
170	
171	# counts back onto bursts
172	nh = fdf[fdf.type == "halo"].groupby("nickname").size()
173	nc = fdf[fdf.type == "cluster"].groupby("nickname").size()
174	bdf["n_foreground_halo"] = bdf.nickname.map(nh).fillna(0).astype(int)
175	bdf["n_foreground_cluster"] = bdf.nickname.map(nc).fillna(0).astype(int)
176	
177	# ---------- Sheet2 cross-check of counts ----------

## Verification status of the foreground counts

**What I could verify from the sheet itself** — and the news is mixed:

✅ **Geometry is internally valid.** Recomputing impact = θ_sep × D_A(z_phot) (Planck18) reproduces every listed `Impact_Parmeter_kpc` to ratio ≈ 1.000. So the impact numbers are arithmetically correct *given* the listed coordinates and photo-z. (One 1.03 outlier, phineas obj `194031778315722893`, is just a truncated-Dec scientific-notation leak in the sheet — cosmetic.)

⚠️ **27 of 49 entries fail a sanity flag** (`flags` column in `foreground.csv`):
- **`ZPHOT_GE_ZHOST` (11 halos/clusters):** the object's photo-z is *≥* the FRB host's spec-z — it can't be foreground by point estimate. Hits whitney (3 of 4 halos), wilhelm (its only halo), phineas, chromatica, casey (5 of 9 halos). **But the sheet has no photo-z errors**, so these can't be definitively ruled background either.
- **`IMPACT_GT_R500` (12 of 15 clusters):** impact 600–5700 kpc vs cluster R500 only 500–850 kpc — the sightline passes up to ~10× R500 *outside* the cluster. Only **one** cluster (phineas J115120.4+714435, b/R500 ≈ 0.83) is actually pierced. The "intervening cluster" list is mostly clusters-in-the-field, not clusters the FRB sightline crosses.
- **`HOST_Z_UNKNOWN` (2):** freya's halos — freya has no spec-z, so foreground is undecidable.

Net: only **~22 of 49** (21 halos + 1 cluster) survive the internal foreground + geometry cuts. Also confirmed: **Sheet2's cluster column is misaligned** — don't use it for attribution; `foreground.csv` is built from Sheet1.

**What I cannot verify without external catalogs** (the sheet doesn't contain it):
1. Does each `obj_ID` actually exist at those coords in the cited survey? (WISE×PS1 STRM, Legacy DR8 Zhou+2021, Wen+ DESI/WISE cluster catalog)
2. Photo-z **uncertainties** — required to adjudicate the 11 borderline `ZPHOT_GE_ZHOST` cases.
3. Galaxy vs star/QSO classification (the `prob_gal/star/qso`, `class` columns).
4. Halo virial radii (no halo mass in the sheet) — so "halo intersected" can't be checked the way clusters can.

To close items 1–4 I'd cross-match each object against VizieR/NED via astroquery (needs network). Two ways: a deterministic astroquery script, or a fan-out workflow (one verifier agent per object, adversarially checking existence + z + classification). Which do you want — and should I start with just the 22 survivors or all 49?

One loose end from earlier: `CLAUDE.md` still references the nonexistent `chimedsa_burst_specs.csv` as the nickname↔TNS map. That map now genuinely exists as `bursts.csv`, but it's in `scratch/` (WIP). I'll fix the CLAUDE.md pointer once we settle a canonical home — flagging it as decision-pending rather than pointing docs at a scratch path.

Exit non-zero on any failure.\n\"\"\"\n\nimport os\nimport sys\n\nimport numpy as np\nimport pandas as pd\n\nHERE = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))\nSRC = os.path.join(HERE, \"source\")\nS2 = os.path.join(SRC, \"DSA110_CHIME_Codetection_BurstProperties_Foreground  - Sheet2.csv\")\nS3 = os.path.join(SRC, \"DSA110_CHIME_Codetection_BurstProperties_Foreground  - Sheet3.csv\")\n\nbursts = pd.read_csv(os.path.join(HERE, \"bursts.csv\"))\nfg = pd.read_csv(os.path.join(HERE, \"foreground.csv\"))\n\nfails = []\n\n\ndef close(a, b, tol=1e-6):\n    if pd.isna(a) and pd.isna(b):\n        return True\n    try:\n        return abs(float(a) - float(b)) <= tol * max(1.0, abs(float(b)))\n    except (TypeError, ValueError):\n        return str(a).strip() == str(b).strip()\n\n\n# ---- bursts vs Sheet3 (keyed by TNS) ----\ns3 = pd.read_csv(S3, header=0, dtype=str)\ns3.columns = [\"tns\", \"mjd\", \"loc\", \"ra_deg\", \"dec_deg\", \"z_spec\"]\ns3 = s3.set_index(s3.tns.str.strip())\nn_burst_checks = 0\nfor _, b in bursts.iterrows():\n    o = s3.loc[b.tns.strip()]\n    for col, ocol in [(\"mjd\", \"mjd\"), (\"ra_deg\", \"ra_deg\"), (\"dec_deg\", \"dec_deg\"),\n                      (\"z_spec\", \"z_spec\")]:\n        ov = float(o[ocol]) if str(o[ocol]).strip() not in (\"\", \"nan\") else np.nan\n        if not close(b[col], ov, tol=1e-4):\n            fails.append(f\"BURST {b.nickname} {col}: out={b[col]} vs Sheet3={ov}\")\n        n_burst_checks += 1\nassert len(bursts) == 12, f\"expected 12 bursts, got {len(bursts)}\"\nassert set(bursts.tns.str.strip()) == set(s3.index), \"burst TNS set != Sheet3 TNS set\"\n\n# ---- foreground vs Sheet2 (keyed by obj id / obj name) ----\ns2 = pd.read_csv(S2, header=None, dtype=str).fillna(\"\")\noracle = {}  # key -> (impact, ra, dec, zphot)\nfor i in range(1, len(s2)):\n    r = s2.iloc[i]\n    if r[13].strip() or r[14].strip():  # halo: obj_ID col 14\n        oracle[(\"halo\", r[14].strip())] = (r[15], r[16], r[17], r[18])\n    if r[24].strip():  # cluster: obj_name col 24\n        oracle[(\"cluster\", r[24].strip())] = (r[26], r[27], r[28], r[29])\n\nn_fg_checks = 0\nfor _, e in fg.iterrows():\n    key = (e.type, str(e.obj).strip())\n    if key not in oracle:\n        fails.append(f\"FG {e.nickname}/{e.type} obj={e.obj}: not found in Sheet2 oracle\")\n        continue\n    imp, ra, dec, zp = oracle[key]\n    for val, ov, name in [(e.impact_kpc_listed, imp, \"impact\"), (e.ra_deg, ra, \"ra\"),\n                          (e.dec_deg, dec, \"dec\"), (e.z_phot, zp, \"zphot\")]:\n        ovf = float(ov) if str(ov).strip() not in (\"\", \"nan\") else np.nan\n        if not close(val, ovf, tol=1e-3):\n            fails.append(f\"FG {e.nickname}/{e.type} obj={e.obj} {name}: out={val} vs Sheet2={ovf}\")\n        n_fg_checks += 1\n\n# set equality: same objects in both representations\nout_halos = set(fg[fg.type == \"halo\"].obj.astype(str).str.strip())\nora_halos = {k[1] for k in oracle if k[0] == \"halo\"}\nout_cl = set(fg[fg.type == \"cluster\"].obj.astype(str).str.strip())\nora_cl = {k[1] for k in oracle if k[0] == \"cluster\"}\nif out_halos != ora_halos:\n    fails.append(f\"HALO set diff: only-out={out_halos - ora_halos} only-S2={ora_halos - out_halos}\")\nif out_cl != ora_cl:\n    fails.append(f\"CLUSTER set diff: only-out={out_cl - ora_cl} only-S2={ora_cl - out_cl}\")\n\nprint(f\"burst field checks: {n_burst_checks}  (12 bursts x 4 fields vs Sheet3)\")\nprint(f\"foreground value checks: {n_fg_checks}  ({len(fg)} objects x 4 fields vs Sheet2)\")\nprint(f\"halo set: out={len(out_halos)} oracle={len(ora_halos)} equal={out_halos == ora_halos}\")\nprint(f\"cluster set: out={len(out_cl)} oracle={len(ora_cl)} equal={out_cl == ora_cl}\")\nif fails:\n    print(f\"\\nFAILED ({len(fails)}):\")\n    for x in fails:\n        print(\"  \" + x)\n    sys.exit(1)\nprint(\"\\nALL CROSS-CHECKS PASS\")\n"
}

> DEVELOPER

Can you explain what you mean that 27 out of 49 foreground entries were flagged? Flagged for what reason, if not that they were checked, because you mentioned that they still need an external catalog confirmation? Is that because the other fraction of the foreground entries had already been confirmed, or were they a subset flagged for a different reason?

> AGENT

Right to push on this — "flagged" does **not** mean "checked and failed," and "unflagged" does **not** mean "confirmed." Nothing has been externally confirmed yet. Let me be precise.

The flags are **internal red-flag tests** I computed purely from the spreadsheet's own numbers (coords, redshifts, R500). They can only *disqualify* or *mark undecidable* — they can't *qualify*. So the 49 split into:

- **27 flagged** = tripped at least one red flag (something is wrong or unprovable on the face of the data)
- **22 unflagged** = tripped no red flag = *internally self-consistent*, i.e. "not contradicted by the sheet" — **not** "verified against a catalog"

Both groups still need external confirmation. The 22 just have no obvious internal problem; the 27 have a specific one.

The three flag reasons:

1. **`ZPHOT_GE_ZHOST` (11 entries)** — the object's photometric redshift is *≥* the FRB host's spectroscopic redshift. A foreground intervener must sit *in front of* the host (lower z); these don't, by point estimate. Caveat: the sheet gives **no photo-z error bars**, so a marginal case (e.g. 0.557 vs host 0.479) can't be definitively called background — it's "fails the point-estimate test, needs the uncertainty to adjudicate."

2. **`IMPACT_GT_R500` (12 of 15 clusters)** — the sightline's impact parameter is *larger than the cluster's own R500 radius* (often 4–10× larger). The FRB beam passes well outside the cluster, so "intervening cluster" is dubious — it's a cluster *in the field*, not one the sightline pierces. Only 1 cluster (phineas J115120) is actually within R500.

3. **`HOST_Z_UNKNOWN` (2, freya's halos)** — freya has no host spec-z, so "is it foreground?" is undecidable, not pass or fail.

(27 distinct rows because one phineas cluster trips both #1 and #2.)

So to your question directly: the other ~22 were **not** independently confirmed — they're the subset that *survived* the internal cuts. The geometry cross-check I ran earlier proved the *numbers are internally consistent* (impact = θ·D_A(z_phot)), but that's self-consistency, not existence/classification. To actually confirm any entry — flagged or not — I still need to hit the external catalogs (object exists at those coords, real photo-z + error, galaxy vs star/QSO). That external step is what's outstanding for all 49.

> DEVELOPER

Got it. We're still going to try and validate all 49 foreground entries. Is that what you mean?

> AGENT

Yes. All 49 — flagged and unflagged alike — get the external-catalog check. The internal flags just tell us where to expect trouble; they don't exempt anything from confirmation.

Concretely, validating each entry = confirming three things the spreadsheet can't:
1. **Existence** — the `obj_ID` resolves to a real source at the listed RA/Dec in its cited survey (WISE×PS1 STRM, Legacy DR8 / Zhou+2021, or Wen+ DESI/WISE for clusters).
2. **Redshift** — the catalog's photo-z (and its **error**, which the sheet omits) matches; this is what finally adjudicates the 11 `ZPHOT_GE_ZHOST` cases.
3. **Classification** — it's actually a galaxy (not star/QSO), per the catalog.

Outcome per entry: `confirmed` / `refuted` / `inconclusive`, written back as new columns in `foreground.csv`.

Before I start, two choices:

}

> AGENT

Schema resolved. The key win: `ls_dr9.photo_z` has `z_phot_mean`, `z_phot_std`, `z_phot_median`, **and `z_spec`** (joinable to `ls_dr9.tractor` for coords + morphological `type`) — that `z_phot_std` is exactly the photo-z error the spreadsheet omitted, which adjudicates the `ZPHOT_GE_ZHOST` flags. And `desi_dr1.zpix` gives spec-z (`z`, `zerr`, `zwarn`, `spectype`) via `mean_fiber_ra/dec`.

Plan locked. Three confirmed-reachable engines, matched by **coordinates** (the sheet's small obj_IDs are per-FRB row indices, not catalog IDs, so ID matching won't work):
- **ls_dr9** (tractor⋈photo_z) → existence, photo-z ± std, z_spec, morphology — primary for halos
- **desi_dr1.zpix** → spec-z when available (authoritative)
- **NED** → existence, z, type — primary for clusters + galaxy cross-check

(within 1 sigma)\n  host z unknown or no catalog match -> inconclusive\nRead-only public queries; writes foreground_validated.csv next to this script.\n\"\"\"\n\nimport os\nimport socket\nimport    return rows[i], float(sep[i])\n\n\ndef q_lsdr9(ra, dec, rad_as):\n    rad = rad_as / 3600.0\n    q = (\n        \"SELECT t.ra, t.dec, t.type, p.z_phot_mean, p.z_phot_std, p.z_phot_median, p.z_spec    row, sep = _nearest(r, ra, dec, \"ra\", \"dec\")\n    if row is None:\n        return {}\n    return dict(lsdr9_sep_as=round(sep, 2), lsdr9_type=str(row[\"type\"]).strip(),\n               lsdr9_zphot=float(row[\"z_phot_mean\"]), lsdr9_zphot_std=float(row[\"z_phot_std\"]),\n               lsdr9_zspec=(float(row[\"z_spec\"]) if row[\"z_spec\"] is not None\n                            and float(row[\"z_spec\"]) > -90 else np.nan))\n\n\ndef q_desi(ra, dec, rad_as):\n    rad = rad_as / 3600.0\n    q = (\n        \"SELECT mean_fiber_ra, mean_fiber_dec, z, zerr, zwarn, spectype \"\n        \"FROM desi_dr1.zpix \"\n        f\"WHERE 't' = q3c_radial_query(mean_fiber_ra, mean_fiber_dec, {ra}, {dec}, {rad}) \"\n        \"AND zwarn = 0\"\n    )\n    r = TAP.search(q).to_table()\n    row, sep = _nearest(r, ra, dec, \"mean_fiber_ra\", \"mean_fiber_dec\")\n    if row is None:\n        return {}\n    return dict(desi_sep_as=round(sep, 2), desi_specz=float(row[\"z\"]),\n                desi_zerr=float(row[\"zerr\"]), desi_spectype=str(row[\"spectype\"]).strip())\n\n\ndef q_ned(ra, dec, rad_as):\n    from astroquery.ipac.ned import Ned\n    t = Ned.query_region(SkyCoord(ra * u.deg, dec * u.deg), radius=rad_as * u.arcsec)\n    if t is None or len(t) == 0:\n        return {}\n    row, sep = _nearest(t, ra, dec, \"RA\", \"DEC\")\n    z = row[\"Redshift\"]\n    return dict(ned_sep_as=round(sep, 2), ned_name=str(row[\"Object Name\"]).strip(),\n                ned_type=str(row[\"Type\"]).strip(),\n                ned_z=(float(z) if z is not None and not np.ma.is_masked(z) else np.nan))\n\n\ndef best_z_and_verdict(host_z, sheet_zphot, d):\n    \"\"\"Pick best redshift; return (best_z, source, verdict).\"\"\"\n    # priority: DESI spec-z > LS z_spec > LS z_phot(+std) > NED z\n    if not np.isnan(d.get(\"desi_specz\", np.nan)):\n        bz, src, std = d[\"desi_specz\"], \"desi_specz\", 0.0\n    elif not np.isnan(d.get(\"lsdr9_zspec\", np.nan)):\n        bz, src, std = d[\"lsdr9_zspec\"], \"lsdr9_zspec\", 0.0\n    elif not np.isnan(d.get(\"lsdr9_zphot\", np.nan)):\n        bz, src, std = d[\"lsdr9_zphot\"], \"lsdr9_zphot\", \"inconclusive\"\n    if np.isnan(host_z):\n        return bz, src, \"inconclusive\"  # cannot judge foreground without host z\n    if std == 0.0:  # spec-z\n        return bz, src, (\"confirmed\" if bz < host_z else \"refuted\")\n    if np.isnan(std):\n        return bz, src, (\"confirmed\" if bz < host_z else \"refuted\")\n    if bz + std < host_z:\n        return bz, src, \"confirmed\"\n    if bz - std > host_z:\n        return bz, src, \"refuted\"\n    return bz, src, \"inconclusive\"\n\n\nout = []\nfor i, e in fg.iterrows():\n    rad = CLU_RADIUS_AS if e.type == \"cluster\" else > AGENT

ADQL geometry isn't translated by Data Lab's backend (passes `POINT` through to nonexistent PostgreSQL `point()`), and bare q3c trips the ADQL parser. Cleanest portable fix: a pure ra/dec **bounding box** in the WHERE (with a cos(dec) correction on ra, since these are at dec ≈ 72°), then enforce the exact radius in Python via the separation I already compute. No geometry functions at all.

{
  "replace_all": false,
  "file_path": "/Users/jakobfaber/Developer/repos/github.com/jakobtfaber/dsa110-FLITS/scratch/codetection/validate_foreground.py",
  "old_string": "def _nearest(rows, ra, dec, racol, deccol):\n    \"\"\"Return (row, sep_arcsec) of the nearest row to (ra,dec), or (None, nan).\"\"\"\n    if rows is None or len(rows) == 0:\n        return None, np.nan\n    c0 = SkyCoord(ra * u.deg, dec * u.deg)\n    cs = SkyCoord(np.asarray(rows[racol], float) * u.deg, np.asarray(rows[deccol], float) * u.deg)\n    sep = c0.separation(cs).arcsec\n    i = int(np.argmin(sep))\n    return rows[i], float(sep[i])\n\n\ndef q_lsdr9(ra, dec, rad_as):\n    rad = rad_as / 3600.0\n    q = (\n        \"SELECT t.ra, t.dec, t.type, p.z_phot_mean, p.z_phot_std, p.z_phot_median, p.z_spec \"\n        \"FROM ls_dr9.tractor t JOIN ls_dr9.photo_z p ON t.ls_id = p.ls_id \"\n        f\"WHERE CONTAINS(POINT('ICRS', t.ra, t.dec), CIRCLE('ICRS', {ra}, {dec}, {rad})) = 1\"\n    )",
  "new_string": "def _nearest(rows, ra, dec, racol, deccol, rad_as=None):\n    \"\"\"Return (row, sep_arcsec) of nearest row within rad_as, or (None, nan).\n\n    Data Lab's ADQL backend does not translate POINT/CIRCLE geometry and rejects\n    bare q3c in WHERE, so the SQL uses a cheap ra/dec bounding box; the true cone\n    cut is enforced here on the exact angular separation.\n    \"\"\"\n    if rows is None or len(rows) == 0:\n        return None, np.nan\n    c0 = SkyCoord(ra * u.deg, dec * u.deg)\n    cs = SkyCoord(np.asarray(rows[racol], float) * u.deg, np.asarray(rows[deccol], float) * u.deg)\n    sep = c0.separation(cs).arcsec\n    i = int(np.argmin(sep))\n    if rad_as is not None and sep[i] > rad_as:\n        return None, np.nan\n    return rows[i], float(sep[i])\n\n\ndef _bbox(ra, dec, rad_as):\n    ddec = rad_as / 3600.0\n    dra = ddec / max(np.cos(np.deg2rad(dec)), 0.02)\n    return ra - dra, ra + dra, dec - ddec, dec + ddec\n\n\ndef q_lsdr9(ra, dec, rad_as):\n    r0, r1, d0, d1 = _bbox(ra, dec, rad_as)\n    q = (\n        \"SELECT t.ra, t.dec, t.type, p.z_phot_mean, p.z_phot_std, p.z_phot_median, p.z_spec \"\n        \"FROM ls_dr9.tractor t JOIN ls_dr9.photo_z p ON t.ls_id = p.ls_id \"\n        f\"WHERE t.dec BETWEEN {d0} AND {d1} AND t.ra BETWEEN {r0} AND {r1}\"\n    )"
}

  "new_string": "def q_simbad(ra, dec, rad_as):\n    # Best-effort secondary classification; SIMBAD is sparse for faint photo-z galaxies.\n    # Defensive: votable-field names differ across astroquery versions -> never raise.\n    from astroquery.simbad import Simbad\n\n    s = Simbad()\n    for fld in ((\"otype\", \"rvz_redshift\"), (\"otype\", \"rv_value\"), ()):\n        try:\n            if fld:\n                s.add_votable_fields(*fld)\n            break\n        except Exception:\n            s = Simbad()\n    t = s.query_region(SkyCoord(ra * u.deg, dec * u.deg), radius=rad_as * u.arcsec)\n    if t is None or len(t) == 0:\n        return {}\n    racol = \"ra\" if \"ra\" in t.colnames else \"RA\"\n    deccol = \"dec\" if \"dec\" in t.colnames else \"DEC\"\n    try:\n        row, sep = _nearest(t, ra, dec, racol, deccol, rad_as)\n    except Exception:\n        row, sep = t[0], np.nan\n    if row is None:\n        return {}\n    otype = next((str(row[c]) for c in (\"otype\", \"OTYPE\") if c in t.colnames), \"\")\n    zc = next((c for c in (\"rvz_redshift\", \"z_value\", \"RVZ_REDSHIFT\") if c in t.colnames), None)\n    sz = np.nan\n    if zc is not None and row[zc] is not None and not np.ma.is_masked(row[zc]):\n        try:\n            sz = float(row[zc])\n        except (TypeError, ValueError):\n            sz = np.nan\n    return dict(simbad_sep_as=(round(sep, 2) if sep == sep else np.nan),\n                simbad_otype=otype.strip(), simbad_z=sz)\n\n\ndef best_z_and_verdict(host_z, sheet_zphot, d):\n    \"\"\"Pick best redshift; return (best_z, source, verdict).\"\"\""
}

> AGENT

Audit looks healthy: ls_dr9 matches at median 0.01″ (39/49), NED at 0.24″ (47/49) — these are the *same* sources the sheet listed, so the redshift comparisons are valid. Only one halo (phineas `194031778315722893`, the truncated-Dec entry) matched at 2.44″ — already suspect from the sci-notation leak. The 13 inconclusive are mostly the 9 `WISE,PS1,STRM` halos with no z in any of these engines (they need the PS1-STRM catalog by objID).

Now an independent verifier for the validation — re-derives every verdict from the recorded catalog values (independent of the script's own logic) and re-queries a sample to confirm the redshifts reproduce. Cleaning scaffolding first:

  "content": "\"\"\"Independent check of validate_foreground.py output (foreground_validated.csv).\n\nA) LOGIC (offline, deterministic): re-derive every foreground_verdict from the\n   recorded catalog columns using a from-scratch reimplementation of the decision\n   rule, and assert it agrees with the script's verdict for all 49 rows. Catches\n   coding/transcription bugs in the original rule.\nB) MATCH QUALITY (offline): assert every confirmed/refuted verdict rests on a\n   catalog match close enough to be the SAME source the sheet listed\n   (lsdr9/ned < 3\", desi-halo < 5\"); a far match would mean we judged the wrong object.\nC) REPRODUCE (online): independently re-query the catalog that produced best_z for a\n   sample of objects via a fresh service call and assert the redshift reproduces.\nExit non-zero on any disagreement.\n\"\"\"\n\nimport os\nimport socket\nimport sys\nimport warnings\n\nwarnings.filterwarnings(\"ignore\")\nsocket.setdefaulttimeout(90)\n\nimport numpy as np\nimport pandas as pd\n\nHERE = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))\nv = pd.read_csv(os.path.join(HERE, \"foreground_validated.csv\"))\nfails = []\n\n\ndef nn(x):\n    return x is not None and not (isinstance(x, float) and np.isnan(x))\n\n\n# ---- A) independent verdict re-derivation ----\ndef rederive(r):\n    host = r.host_z_spec\n    # priority must match the documented rule: desi spec > ls zspec > ls zphot > ned z\n    if nn(r.desi_specz):\n        z, std, spec = r.desi_specz, 0.0, True\n    elif nn(r.lsdr9_zspec):\n        z, std, spec = r.lsdr9_zspec, 0.0, True\n    elif nn(r.lsdr9_zphot):\n        z, std, spec = r.lsdr9_zphot, r.lsdr9_zphot_std, False\n    elif nn(r.ned_z):\n        z, std, spec = r.ned_z, np.nan, False\n    else:\n        return \"inconclusive\"\n    if not nn(host):\n        return \"inconclusive\"\n    if spec or not nn(std):\n        return \"confirmed\" if z < host else \"refuted\"\n    if z + std < host:\n        return \"confirmed\"\n    if z - std > host:\n        return \"refuted\"\n    return \"inconclusive\"\n\n\nfor _, r in v.iterrows():\n    mine = rederive(r)\n    if mine != r.foreground_verdict:\n        fails.append(f\"VERDICT {r.nickname}/{r.obj}: script={r.foreground_verdict} indep={mine}\")\n\n# ---- B) match-quality: verdict must rest on a near match ----\nfor _, r in v.iterrows():\n    if r.foreground_verdict not in (\"confirmed\", \"refuted\"):\n        continue\n    src = r.best_z_source\n    sep, lim = None, None\n    if src in (\"lsdr9_zphot\", \"lsdr9_zspec\"):\n        sep, lim = r.lsdr9_sep_as, 3.0\n    elif src == \"desi_specz\":\n        sep, lim = r.desi_sep_as, (90.0 if r.type == \"cluster\" else 5.0)\n    elif src == \"ned_z\":\n        sep, lim = r.ned_sep_as, 5.0\n    if sep is None or np.isnan(sep) or sep > lim:\n        fails.append(f\"MATCH {r.nickname}/{r.obj}: verdict {r.foreground_verdict} on {src} \"\n                     f\"sep={sep} > limit {lim} (possible wrong source)\")\n\n# ---- C) reproduce a sample online via independent queries ----\nimport pyvo\nfrom astropy.coordinates import SkyCoord\nfrom astropy import units as u\n\nTAP = pyvo.dal.TAPService(\"https://datalab.noirlab.edu/tap\")\n\n\ndef reget_desi(ra, dec):\n    q = (\"SELECT z, zwarn FROM desi_dr1.zpix \"\n         f\"WHERE mean_fiber_dec BETWEEN {dec - 0.0014} AND {dec + 0.0014} \"\n         f\"AND mean_fiber_ra BETWEEN {ra - 0.0045} AND {ra + 0.0045} AND zwarn=0\")\n    t = TAP.search(q).to_table()\n    return None if len(t) == 0 else float(t[\"z\"][int(np.argmin(np.abs(np.asarray(t[\"z\"]))))])\n\n\ndef reget_lsphot(ra, dec):\n    q = (\"SELECT p.z_phot_mean FROM ls_dr9.tractor t JOIN ls_dr9.photo_z p ON t.ls_id=p.ls_id \"\n         f\"WHERE t.dec BETWEEN {dec - 0.0008} AND {dec + 0.0008} \"\n         f\"AND t.ra BETWEEN {ra - 0.0028} AND {ra + 0.0028}\")\n    t = TAP.search(q).to_table()\n    return None if len(t) == 0 else float(t[\"z_phot_mean\"][0])\n\n\n# sample: one confirmed cluster (desi), one refuted halo (lsphot), one confirmed halo (desi)\nsample = []\nfor src_kind, verdict in [(\"desi_specz\", \"confirmed\"), (\"lsdr9_zphot\", \"refuted\"),\n                          (\"desi_specz\", \"confirmed\")]:\n    sub = v[(v.best_z_source == src_kind) & (v.foreground_verdict == verdict)]\n    sub = sub[~sub.obj.astype(str).isin([s[0] for s in sample])]\n    if len(sub):\n        sample.append((str(sub.iloc[0].obj), sub.iloc[0]))\n\nn_repro = 0\nfor obj, r in sample:\n    try:\n        if r.best_z_source == \"desi_specz\":\n            got = reget_desi(r.ra_deg, r.dec_deg)\n            ref = r.desi_specz\n        else:\n            got = reget_lsphot(r.ra_deg, r.dec_deg)\n            ref = r.lsdr9_zphot\n        ok = got is not None and abs(got - ref) < 0.02\n        n_repro += 1\n        print(f\"REPRODUCE {r.nickname}/{obj} {r.best_z_source}: stored={ref:.4f} requery={got} ok={ok}\")\n        if not ok:\n            fails.append(f\"REPRODUCE {r.nickname}/{obj}: stored={ref} requery={got}\")\n    except Exception as ex:\n        fails.append(f\"REPRODUCE {r.nickname}/{obj}: {ex.__class__.__name__}: {str(ex)[:80]}\")\n\nprint(f\"\\nverdict re-derivations checked: {len(v)}\")\nprint(f\"match-quality checks on confirmed/refuted: {(v.foreground_verdict != 'inconclusive').sum()}\")\nprint(f\"online reproduce checks: {n_repro}\")\nif fails:\n    print(f\"\\nFAILED ({len(fails)}):\")\n    for x in fails:\n        print(\"  \" + x)\n    sys.exit(1)\nprint(\"\\nALL VALIDATION CHECKS PASS\")\n"
}

ddec} AND {dec + ddec} AND ra BETWEEN {ra - dra} AND {ra + dra}\")\n    t = svc.search(q).to_table()\n    return f\"{len(t)} rows\" + (f\" types={list(t['type'])}\" if len(t) else \"\")\n\n\ndef sdss(ra, dec):\n    from astroquery.sdss import SDSS\n    c = SkyCoord(ra * u.deg, dec * u.deg)\n    try:\n        t = SDSS.query_region(c, radius=5 * u.arcsec,\n                              photoobj_fields=[\"ra\", \"dec\", \"type\", \"z\"], spectro=False)\n        return \"None\" if t is None else f\"{len(t)} rows cols={list(t.colnames)}\"\n    except Exception as e:\n        return f\"ERR {e.__class__.__name__}: {str(e)[:60]}\"\n\n\ndef desi_wide(ra, dec, rad_as):\n    ddec = rad_as / 3600.0\n    dra = ddec / max(np.cos(np.deg2rad(dec)), 0.02)\n    q = (\"SELECT z, spectype FROM desi_dr1.zpix \"\n         f\"WHERE mean_fiber_dec BETWEEN {dec - ddec} AND {dec + ddec} \"\n         f\"AND mean_fiber_ra BETWEEN {ra - dra} AND {ra + dra} AND zwarn=0\")\n    t = svc.search(q).to_table()\n    return f\"{len(t)} rows\" + (f\" {list(zip(t['z'], t['spectype']))[:4]}\" if len(t) else \"\")\n\n\nfor nm, ra, dec, zsheet in targets:\n    print(f\"\\n==== {nm}  ({ra},{dec})  sheet z_phot={zsheet} ====\")\n    print(\" VizieR :\", vizier_strm(ra, dec))\n    print(\" LStract:\", ls_tractor_only(ra, dec, 5), \"| 15as:\", ls_tractor_only(ra, dec, 15))\n    print(\" SDSS   :\", sdss(ra, dec))\n    print(\" DESI20 :\", desi_wide(ra, dec, 20))\n"

This script does what IS possible from accessible services:\n  - confirm each is a real PS1 source at the sheet objID (MAST PanSTARRS DR2, best effort)\n  - document the Legacy-footprint gap per object (Data Lab tractor count within 60\")\n  - leave the foreground verdict honestly 'inconclusive-no-independent-z' (not fabricated)\nWrites ps1_strm_resolution.csv.\n\"\"\"\n\nimport os\nimport socket\nimport warnings\n\nwarnings.filterwarnings(\"ignore\")\nsocket.setdefaulttimeout(120)\n\nimport numpy as np\nimport pandas as pd\nimport pyvo\nfrom astropy import units as u\n\nHERE = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))\nfg = pd.read_csv(os.path.join(HERE, \"foreground.csv\"))\nval = pd.read_csv(os.path.join(HERE, \"foreground_validated.csv\"))\n\n# the 9 STRM halos that are inconclusive with no catalog z\nstrm = fg[fg.survey.fillna(\"\").str.contains(\"STRM\")].copy()\ninconc = set(val[(val.foreground_verdict == \"inconclusive\")\n                 & (val.best_z_source == \"none\")].obj.astype(str))\nstrm = strm[strm.obj.astype(str).isin(inconc)]\n\nsvc = pyvo.dal.TAPService(\"https://datalab.noirlab.edu/tap\")\n\n\ndef legacy_count(ra, dec, rad_as=60.0):\n    ddec = rad_as / 3600.0\n    dra = ddec / max(np.cos(np.deg2rad(dec)), 0.02)\n    q = (\"SELECT COUNT(*) AS n FROM ls_dr9.tractor \"\n         f\"WHERE dec BETWEEN {dec - ddec} AND {dec + ddec} AND ra BETWEEN {ra - dra} AND {ra + dra}\")\n    return int(svc.search(q).to_table()[\"n\"][0])\n\n\ndef ps1_confirm(ra, dec, objid):\n    from astroquery.mast import Catalogs\n    try:\n        t = Catalogs.query_region(\n            f\"{ra} {dec}\", radius=3 * u.arcsec, catalog=\"Panstarrs\",\n            data_release=\"dr2\", table=\"mean\", columns=[\"objID\", \"raMean\", \"decMean\"])\n        if t is None or len(t) == 0:\n            return False, np.nan, np.nan\n        ids = [int(x) for x in t[\"objID\"]]\n        match = int(objid) in ids\n        # nearest\n        from astropy.coordinates import SkyCoord\n        c0 = SkyCoord(ra * u.deg, dec * u.deg)\n        cs = SkyCoord(np.asarray(t[\"raMean\"], float) * u.deg, np.asarray(t[\"decMean\"], float) * u.deg)\n        sep = float(np.min(c0.separation(cs).arcsec))\n        return match, sep, len(t)\n    except Exception as ex:\n        return f\"ERR:{ex.__class__.__name__}\", np.nan, np.nan\n\n\nrows = []\nfor _, e in strm.iterrows():\n    lc = legacy_count(e.ra_deg, e.dec_deg)\n    objmatch, sep, npix = ps1_confirm(e.ra_deg, e.dec_deg, e.obj)\n    rows.append(dict(\n        nickname=e.nickname, obj=e.obj, ra_deg=e.ra_deg, dec_deg=e.dec_deg,\n        host_z_spec=e.host_z_spec, sheet_zphot=e.z_phot,\n        legacy_sources_within_60as=lc, in_legacy_footprint=(lc > 0),\n        ps1_objid_confirmed=objmatch, ps1_nearest_sep_as=(round(sep, 2) if sep == sep else np.nan),\n        resolution=\"inconclusive-no-independent-z (outside Legacy/DESI/SDSS; PS1-STRM only)\"))\n    print(f\"{e.nickname:11s} obj={str(e.obj):20s} legacy60as={lc} \"\n          f\"ps1_objid_confirmed={objmatch} sep={sep}\")\n\nout = pd.DataFrame(rows)\nout.to_csv(os.path.join(HERE, \"ps1_strm_resolution.csv\"), index=False)\nprint(\"\\n=== SUMMARY (9 STRM halos) ===\")\nprint(\"in Legacy footprint (>0 sources within 60as):\", int(out.in_legacy_footprint.sum()), \"/\", len(out))\nprint(\"PS1 objID confirmed:\", int((out.ps1_objid_confirmed == True).sum()), \"/\", len(out))  # noqa: E712\nprint(\"\\nAll remain: inconclusive-no-independent-z (PS1-STRM photo-z is the only redshift).\")\n"
}

The 9 STRM halos are now resolved as far as accessible catalogs allow. Final adjudication of all 49:

| verdict | n | meaning |
|---|---|---|
| **confirmed foreground** | 29 | catalog z (spec or photo-z±σ) < host z |
| **refuted (background)** | 7 | catalog z ≥ host z — drop from foreground list |
| **inconclusive — borderline** | 4 | Legacy/Zhou photo-z within 1σ of host (whitney 1582, phineas 986/1072, casey 825) |
| **inconclusive — no independent z** | 9 | the STRM halos |

**The 9 STRM halos** (`ps1_strm_resolution.csv`): every one is a **real PS1 source — objID confirmed two ways** (by-position cone *and* direct by-ID lookup, coords matching the sheet to <0.08″). But all 9 have **0 Legacy sources within 60″** — they sit outside the DESI Legacy / SDSS / DESI-spectroscopy footprints entirely. Their only redshift is the PS1-STRM photo-z (the sheet's value), which lives in a MAST HLSP not exposed to cone queries. So: identity and existence are solid; foreground status genuinely can't be adjudicated against an independent redshift. Not fabricating a verdict.

**Net result of the whole exercise** — of the 49 listed foreground objects:
- 29 hold up as foreground;
- 7 are actually background (should be removed);
- 13 unresolved — 4 truly borderline, 9 outside the independent-z footprint;
- plus the standing structural caveats: **14/15 clusters lie outside their own R500** (real foreground objects, but the sightline doesn't pierce them), and the **sheet's photo-z column is unreliable** for several entries (use the catalog values now in `foreground_validated.csv`).

The only way to close the 9 further is direct **PS1-STRM HLSP access** — MAST CasJobs (login) or bulk-download the relevant healpix tiles. That needs credentials / a sizable download, so I'm stopping here rather than spiral on auth. Want me to set that up, or is objID+existence confirmation enough for those 9?

Final files in `scratch/codetection/` (untracked — not committing without your go-ahead): `bursts.csv`, `foreground.csv`, `foreground_validated.csv`, `ps1_strm_resolution.csv`, plus the four generators/verifiers and `source/`.

=== README (cols + format) ===
README file for PS1-STRM - Pan-STARRS1 Source Types and Redshifts with Machine Learning
MAST webpage: https://archive.stsci.edu/hlsp/ps1-strm/
Refer to this HLSP with DOI: http://dx.doi.org/10.17909/t9-rnk7-gr88

## Introduction
PS1-STRM is a neural network source classification and photometric redshift catalog created from the PanSTARRS1 (PS1) 3π DR1.  Neural networks have been trained on a compilation of spectroscopic measurements, cross-matched with PS1.  Based on PS1 forced mean photometry, a source is classified as galaxy, star, quasar, or unsure. For galaxies, photometric redshift estimation is performed, also yielding an estimate of redshift error via Monte-Carlo sampling.  Sources lying outside the parameter coverage of the training set (i.e. extrapolated sources) are identified using self-organizing maps.  Classification and photo-z results are provided for every source in the PS1 3π DR1 ForcedMeanObject table, a total of 2,902,054,648 objects.  See the README file and the primary reference paper for a detailed description of the catalog metadata.

## Data Products
The catalog files are split based on strips of declination, with the following format:
    hlsp_ps1-strm_ps1_gpc1_<decmin>-<decmax>_multi_v1_cat.csv.gz
where:
    <decmin> = Minimum declination this file covers (in degrees).  "m" and "p" represent negative and postive signs.
    <decmax> = Maximum declination this file covers (in degrees).  "m" and "p" represent negative and postive signs.

An example file name that covers a declination range from -2 < dec < +1 degrees is:

    hlsp_ps1-strm_ps1_gpc1_m02-p01_multi_v1_cat.csv.gz

Data file types:
_cat.csv.gz = Portion of the catalog covering a given declination range.

### Catalog Column Descriptions

Note: B20 = Beck et al. (2020), F16 = Flewelling et al. (2016).
---------------------------------------------------
Column Name	    	Data Type	Description
---------------------------------------------------
objID			bigint		The main PS1 source identifier, should be used to match with other PS1 tables (see F16). Not unique.
uniquePspsOBid		bigint		A unique PS1 source identifier, can be used to match with MeanObject and ObjectThin (see F16).
raMean			float		The PS1 J2000 equatorial right ascension coordinate of the source, in degrees (see F16).
decMean			float		The PS1 J2000 equatorial declination coordinate of the source, in degrees (see F16).
l			float		The PS1 J2000 Galactic longitude coordinate of the source, in degrees (see F16).
b			float		The PS1 J2000 Galactic latitude coordinate of the source, in degrees (see F16).
class			varchar[8]	The class assigned to the source, using the fiducial decision boundary b=0.7 (see Sect. 4.1 of B20). Can take the following values: "GALAXY", "STAR", "QSO" or "UNSURE".
prob_Galaxy		float		The probability-like neural network output for the galaxy class. Corresponds to the P_{class} general notation in the text. Refer to Sect. 4.1 of B20 for more details.
prob_Star		float		The probability-like neural network output for the star class. Corresponds to the P_{class} general notation in the text. Refer to Sect. 4.1 of B20 for more details.
prob_QSO		float		The probability-like neural network output for the quasar class. Corresponds to the P_{class} general notation in the text. Refer to Sect. 4.1 of B20 for more details.
extrapolation_Class	int		The extrapolation flag for the classification, 0 if non-extrapolated, 1 if extrapolated. Definition: d_{SOM} > 1.562 (see Sect. 3.3 of B20).
cellDistance_Class	int		The distance to the nearest SOM cell centre in the classification SOM. Denoted d_{SOM} in the text (see Sect. 3.3 of B20).
cellID_Class		int		The identifier of the nearest SOM cell in the classification SOM (see Sect. 3.3 of B20).
z_phot			float		The Monte-Carlo photometric redshift estimate z_{phot}. Slightly less accurate than z_{phot,0}. Refer to Sect. 3.4 and 4.2 of B20 for more details.
z_photErr		float		The calibrated redshift error estimate \tilde{\Delta z}_{phot} = 1.986 \Delta z_{phot}. Refer to Sect. 3.4 and 4.2 of B20 for more details.
z_phot0			float		The base photometric redshift estimate z_{phot,0}. Refer to Sect. 3.4 and 4.2 of B20 for more details.
extrapolation_Photoz	int		The extrapolation flag for the photo-z estimation, 0 if non-extrapolated, 1 if extrapolated. Definition:  d_{SOM} > 1.246 (see Sect. 3.3 of B20).
cellDistance_Photoz	float		The distance to the nearest SOM cell centre in the photo-z SOM. Denoted d_{SOM} in the text (see Sect. 3.3 of B20).
cellID_Photoz		int		The identifier of the nearest SOM cell in the photo-z SOM (see Sect. 3.3 of B20).

{
  "file_path": "/Users/jakobfaber/Developer/repos/github.com/jakobtfaber/dsa110-FLITS/scratch/codetection/ps1_strm_adjudicate.py",
  "content": "\"\"\"Final adjudication of the 9 'WISE,PS1,STRM' halos using the actual PS1-STRM catalog.\n\nSource rows (strm_catalog_rows.csv) were extracted by streaming the PS1-STRM HLSP\ndeclination strip p69-p77 and grepping the 9 objIDs. PS1-STRM (Beck+2020) gives, per\nobjID: class (GALAXY/STAR/QSO/UNSURE @ prob threshold 0.7), prob_Galaxy, z_phot,\nz_photErr (calibrated), z_phot0, and extrapolation_Photoz (1 => photo-z outside the\ntraining coverage, unreliable). This is the redshift + error the spreadsheet omitted.\n\nForeground rule vs FRB host spec-z, only when STRM trusts the source as a galaxy:\n  class != GALAXY                      -> inconclusive-not-galaxy (STRM)\n  extrapolation_Photoz == 1            -> inconclusive-extrapolated-photoz\n  host z unknown                       -> inconclusive-host-z-unknown\n  z_phot + z_photErr < host            -> confirmed foreground\n  z_phot - z_photErr > host            -> refuted (background)\n  else (within 1 sigma)                -> inconclusive-borderline\nAlso records sheet_zphot vs strm_zphot to expose the spreadsheet's STRM photo-z error.\n\"\"\"\n\nimport os\n\nimport numpy as np\nimport pandas as pd\n\nHERE = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))\nstrm = pd.read_csv(os.path.join(HERE, \"strm_catalog_rows.csv\"))\nres = pd.read_csv(os.path.join(HERE, \"ps1_strm_resolution.csv\"))  # has nickname, host_z, sheet_zphot\nres[\"obj\"] = res.obj.astype(\"int64\")\nstrm[\"objID\"] = strm.objID.astype(\"int64\")\nm = res.merge(strm, left_on=\"obj\", right_on=\"objID\", how=\"left\")\n\n\ndef adjudicate(r):\n    if r[\"class\"] != \"GALAXY\":\n        return f\"inconclusive-not-galaxy (STRM class={r['class']}, prob_gal={r.prob_Galaxy:.2f})\"\n    if r.extrapolation_Photoz == 1:\n        return \"inconclusive-extrapolated-photoz (STRM photo-z outside training coverage)\"\n    host = r.host_z_spec\n    z, dz = r.z_phot, r.z_photErr\n    if not np.isfinite(host):\n        return \"inconclusive-host-z-unknown\"\n    if z + dz < host:\n        return \"confirmed\"\n    if z - dz > host:\n        return \"refuted\"\n    return \"inconclusive-borderline (within 1 sigma of host)\"\n\n\nrows = []\nfor _, r in m.iterrows():\n    has_z = r[\"class\"] == \"GALAXY\" and r.z_phot > -90\n    verdict = adjudicate(r)\n    zmis = (abs(r.sheet_zphot - r.z_phot) if has_z and np.isfinite(r.sheet_zphot) else np.nan)\n    rows.append(dict(\n        nickname=r.nickname, obj=r.obj, host_z_spec=r.host_z_spec,\n        sheet_zphot=r.sheet_zphot,\n        strm_class=r[\"class\"], strm_prob_galaxy=round(r.prob_Galaxy, 3),\n        strm_zphot=(r.z_phot if has_z else np.nan),\n        strm_zphoterr=(r.z_photErr if has_z else np.nan),\n        strm_extrapolated=(int(r.extrapolation_Photoz) if r.extrapolation_Photoz > -90 else np.nan),\n        sheet_vs_strm_zphot_diff=(round(zmis, 3) if np.isfinite(zmis) else np.nan),\n        strm_verdict=verdict))\nout = pd.DataFrame(rows)\nout.to_csv(os.path.join(HERE, \"ps1_strm_resolution.csv\"), index=False)\n\nprint(out[[\"nickname\", \"obj\", \"host_z_spec\", \"sheet_zphot\", \"strm_class\",\n           \"strm_zphot\", \"strm_zphoterr\", \"strm_extrapolated\",\n           \"sheet_vs_strm_zphot_diff\", \"strm_verdict\"]].to_string(index=False))\nprint(\"\\n=== STRM-based verdicts ===\")\nprint(out.strm_verdict.apply(lambda s: s.split(\" \")[0]).value_counts().to_string())\nbig = out[out.sheet_vs_strm_zphot_diff > 0.05]\nprint(f\"\\nsheet z_phot disagrees with PS1-STRM by >0.05 for {len(big)}/\"\n      f\"{out.sheet_vs_strm_zphot_diff.notna().sum()} galaxies with a STRM photo-z:\")\nprint(big[[\"nickname\", \"obj\", \"sheet_zphot\", \"strm_zphot\", \"sheet_vs_strm_zphot_diff\"]]\n      .to_string(index=False))\nprint(f\"\\nSTRM classifies {(out.strm_class != 'GALAXY').sum()}/9 as non-galaxy (UNSURE).\")\n"
}

  "content": "\"\"\"Independent verification of the PS1-STRM adjudication (ps1_strm_resolution.csv).\n\nThree orthogonal checks:\n A) COLUMN EXTRACTION: re-parse the full 19-column raw rows (strm_catalog_rows_full.csv,\n    schema = README order) and assert class/z_phot/z_photErr/prob_Galaxy/extrap match the\n    cut-column file the adjudicator used. Catches an off-by-one in the `cut -f` extraction\n    (i.e. proves z_phot really is column 14, not a neighbour).\n B) OBJECT IDENTITY: assert each STRM row's own (raMean,decMean) is within 1\" of the sheet\n    coordinates for that objID (from foreground.csv) -> the grep matched the right source.\n C) VERDICT LOGIC: re-derive strm_verdict from the catalog columns via an independent\n    reimplementation and assert it matches ps1_strm_resolution.csv; check headline counts.\nExit non-zero on any disagreement.\n\"\"\"\n\nimport os\nimport sys\n\nimport numpy as np\nimport pandas as pd\nfrom astropy import units as u\nfrom astropy.coordinates import SkyCoord\n\nHERE = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))\nfull = pd.read_csv(os.path.join(HERE, \"strm_catalog_rows_full.csv\"))\ncut = pd.read_csv(os.path.join(HERE, \"strm_catalog_rows.csv\"))\nres = pd.read_csv(os.path.join(HERE, \"ps1_strm_resolution.csv\"))\nfg = pd.read_csv(os.path.join(HERE, \"foreground.csv\"))\nfg[\"obj\"] = fg.obj.astype(str)\nfails = []\n\n# ---- A) column-extraction correctness: full reparse vs cut file ----\nfull[\"objID\"] = full.objID.astype(\"int64\")\ncut[\"objID\"] = cut.objID.astype(\"int64\")\nfa = full.set_index(\"objID\")\nca = cut.set_index(\"objID\")\nfor oid in ca.index:\n    for col in [\"class\", \"z_phot\", \"z_photErr\", \"prob_Galaxy\", \"extrapolation_Photoz\"]:\n        a, b = fa.loc[oid, col], ca.loc[oid, col]\n        same = (a == b) if isinstance(a, str) else abs(float(a) - float(b)) < 1e-9\n        if not same:\n            fails.append(f\"COLEXTRACT {oid} {col}: full={a} cut={b}\")\n\n# ---- B) object identity: STRM coords vs sheet coords ----\nfor _, r in full.iterrows():\n    srow = fg[fg.obj == str(r.objID)]\n    if srow.empty:\n        fails.append(f\"IDENTITY {r.objID}: not in foreground.csv\")\n        continue\n    s = srow.iloc[0]\n    sep = SkyCoord(s.ra_deg * u.deg, s.dec_deg * u.deg).separation(\n        SkyCoord(r.raMean * u.deg, r.decMean * u.deg)).arcsec\n    if sep > 1.0:\n        fails.append(f\"IDENTITY {r.objID}: STRM row {sep:.2f}as from sheet coords (>1as)\")\n\n# ---- C) verdict re-derivation ----\ndef rederive(r):\n    cls = r[\"class\"]\n    if cls != \"GALAXY\":\n        return \"inconclusive-not-galaxy\"\n    if r.extrapolation_Photoz == 1:\n        return \"inconclusive-extrapolated-photoz\"\n    host = r.host_z_spec\n    if not np.isfinite(host):\n        return \"inconclusive-host-z-unknown\"\n    z, dz = r.z_phot, r.z_photErr\n    if z + dz < host:\n        return \"confirmed\"\n    if z - dz > host:\n        return \"refuted\"\n    return \"inconclusive-borderline\"\n\n\nfa2 = full.set_index(\"objID\")\nfor _, rv in res.iterrows():\n    fr = fa2.loc[int(rv.obj)]\n    merged = pd.Series(dict(**{k: fr[k] for k in\n                              (\"class\", \"extrapolation_Photoz\", \"z_phot\", \"z_photErr\")},\n                            host_z_spec=rv.host_z_spec))\n    indep = rederive(merged)\n    if not str(rv.strm_verdict).startswith(indep):\n        fails.append(f\"VERDICT {rv.obj}: script='{rv.strm_verdict}' indep='{indep}'\")\n\n# headline counts\nn_unsure = (full[\"class\"] != \"GALAXY\").sum()\nn_extrap = ((full[\"class\"] == \"GALAXY\") & (full.extrapolation_Photoz == 1)).sum()\nn_conf = res.strm_verdict.str.startswith(\"confirmed\").sum()\nprint(f\"A) column-extraction checks: {len(ca) * 5} comparisons\")\nprint(f\"B) identity checks: {len(full)} rows vs sheet coords\")\nprint(f\"C) verdict re-derivations: {len(res)}\")\nprint(f\"headline: UNSURE={n_unsure} extrapolated={n_extrap} confirmed-foreground={n_conf}\")\nassert n_unsure == 4 and n_extrap == 2 and n_conf == 0, \"headline counts changed!\"\nif fails:\n    print(f\"\\nFAILED ({len(fails)}):\")\n    for x in fails:\n        print(\"  \" + x)\n    sys.exit(1)\nprint(\"\\nALL STRM ADJUDICATION CHECKS PASS\")\n"
}

**Final adjudication — all 49 foreground objects:**

| | confirmed | refuted | inconclusive |
|---|---|---|---|
| clusters (15) | 15 | – | – |
| halos (34) | 14 | 7 | 13 |
| **total** | **29** | **7** | **13** |

All 49 exist in a public catalog. The 13 inconclusive break down as: **4** Legacy/Zhou halos with photo-z within 1σ of host; **9** STRM halos now fully explained by the PS1-STRM catalog itself.

**What going further into PS1-STRM revealed** (the headline): for the 9 STRM halos, the spreadsheet's numbers are not trustworthy —
- **4/9 are not galaxies** per PS1-STRM (class `UNSURE`, prob_Galaxy 0.61–0.69): oran, wilhelm, hamilton (`192943…`), chromatica (`196673…`).
- **2/9 have extrapolated (unreliable) photo-z**: zach, chromatica (`196723…`).
- **The sheet's z_phot is decoupled from the real STRM value** — 4 of the 5 with a STRM photo-z disagree by >0.05, two catastrophically: zach sheet 0.013 vs STRM 0.469; chromatica `196723` sheet 0.041 vs STRM 0.475.

So **none of the 9 STRM halos can be confirmed foreground**, and their spreadsheet entries (both photo-z and, for 4, the galaxy label) are unreliable.

**Three structural caveats stand across the whole table:**
1. 7 halos are genuinely **background** (catalog z ≥ host) — should be removed.
2. **14/15 clusters lie outside their own R500** — real foreground galaxies/BCGs, but the FRB sightline doesn't pierce them.
3. The sheet's `z_phot` column is unreliable broadly; use the catalog values in `foreground_final.csv`. (And Sheet2's cluster column is mis-attributed — only Sheet1/`foreground.csv` is correct.)

**Deliverables** in `scratch/codetection/` (untracked): `foreground_final.csv` (master), `bursts.csv`, plus the staged `foreground.csv` / `foreground_validated.csv` / `ps1_strm_resolution.csv`, the raw STRM evidence (`strm_catalog_rows*.csv`), `source/`, and 5 generators + 5 verifiers. Every generator has a recorded independent cross-check.

what does inconclusive mean?

> AGENT

"Inconclusive" = we couldn't decide **foreground vs background** — not "it's fake" and not "it's background." The object is real; the redshift evidence just isn't decisive enough to place it cleanly in front of or behind the FRB. Three distinct reasons in the 13:

1. **Within 1σ of the host** (4 Legacy/Zhou halos + 1 STRM, hamilton `192963`): the photo-z ± its error straddles the host redshift. E.g. z_phot 0.308 ± 0.073 vs host 0.302 — could be just in front or just behind; the error bar overlaps the host. Can't call it.

2. **Host redshift unknown** (2 freya halos): freya has no spectroscopic z, so "is this object in front of freya?" has no reference to compare against. Undecidable in principle until freya gets a host z.

3. **No trustworthy redshift / not a galaxy** (the other STRM halos): 4 are classed `UNSURE` by PS1-STRM (not confidently galaxies, no photo-z at all), and 2 have *extrapolated* photo-z (the value exists but is flagged unreliable — outside the catalog's training coverage). No usable redshift → can't test foreground.

Contrast with the other two verdicts:
- **confirmed** = best redshift (spec-z, or photo-z+error) is clearly **below** host → in front.
- **refuted** = redshift clearly **above** host → behind (background).
- **inconclusive** = the redshift either straddles the host, or doesn't exist/isn't trustworthy.

So inconclusive is an honest "the data can't say," not a soft fail — and each has a concrete unblock: a spec-z for the object (reasons 1, 3), or a host spec-z for freya (reason 2).

1	\documentclass[twocolumn]{aastex631}
2	
3	\usepackage{amsmath}
4	\usepackage{graphicx}
5	\usepackage{hyperref}
6	
7	\shorttitle{CHIME/FRB and DSA-110 ToA Crossmatching}
8	\shortauthors{Faber et al.}
9	
10	\begin{document}
11	
12	\title{Precision Time-of-Arrival Crossmatching of Fast Radio Bursts between CHIME/FRB and DSA-110}
13	
14	\author[0000-0000-0000-0000]{Josh Faber}
15	\affiliation{Deep Astronomy Group, California Institute of Technology, Pasadena, CA 91125, USA}
16	
17	\begin{abstract}
18	We present a high-precision cross-observatory time-of-arrival (ToA) analysis of 12 Fast Radio Bursts (FRBs) co-detected by the CHIME/FRB and DSA-110 telescopes. By accounting for differential dispersion delays and geometric light-travel time between the two facilities, we measure the residuals between predicted and observed arrival times. Our analysis shows excellent agreement across the sample, with a median residual offset of $2.42 \pm 3.06$ ms. We conduct a systematic search for correlations between ToA residuals and physical burst properties including Dispersion Measure (DM), pulse width (FWHM), measurement uncertainty, and epoch (MJD). We find no statistically significant correlations, demonstrating the robustness of current dispersion modeling and instrumental calibration between the two facilities. A suggestive trend in residuals over time ($p=0.07$) warrants further investigation with larger sample sizes to monitor for potential long-term instrumental drift.
19	\end{abstract}
20	
21	\keywords{Fast radio bursts (529) --- Interstellar medium (847) --- Radio astronomy (1338)}
22	
23	\section{Introduction} \label{sec:intro}
24	
25	Fast Radio Bursts (FRBs) are millisecond-duration radio transients of extragalactic origin \citep{Lorimer2007, Thornton2013}. High-precision timing across multiple observatories is critical for robust localization, interferometic studies, and probing the ionized media through which the signals propagate. The Canadian Hydrogen Intensity Mapping Experiment (CHIME/FRB) and the Deep Synoptic Array (DSA-110) provide complementary coverage in the 400--800 MHz and 1.28--1.53 GHz bands, respectively. Co-detections between these facilities offer unique opportunities to test the $1/\nu^2$ scaling of dispersion delays and verify the relative timing alignment of global radio telescope networks.
26	
27	\section{Methodology} \label{sec:methods}
28	
29	To crossmatch arrival times between CHIME and DSA-110, we must translate arrival times at different central frequencies to a common reference frequency, $\nu_{\text{ref}}$.
30	
31	\subsection{Dispersion Delay Correction}
32	
33	The time delay $\Delta t_{p}$ due to dispersion in a cold plasma is given by:
34	\begin{equation}
35	    \Delta t_{p} = K_{\text{DM}} \cdot \text{DM} \cdot \left( \frac{1}{\nu_{\text{ref}}^2} - \frac{1}{\nu_{\text{obs}}^2} \right)
36	\end{equation}
37	where $K_{\text{DM}} = 4.148808 \times 10^3 \, \text{MHz}^2 \, \text{pc}^{-1} \, \text{cm}^3 \, \text{s}$. In our analysis, we adopt $\nu_{\text{ref}} = 400$ MHz as the canonical reference frequency.
38	
39	\subsection{Geometric Delay Calculation}
40	
41	The light-travel time difference between the two observatories depends on the source coordinates $(\alpha, \delta)$ and the instantaneous orbital positions of the facilities. The predicted geometric delay $\tau_{\text{geo}}$ is calculated as:
42	\begin{equation}
43	    \tau_{\text{geo}} = \frac{(\mathbf{p}_2 - \mathbf{p}_1) \cdot \mathbf{\hat{s}}}{c}
44	\end{equation}
45	where $\mathbf{p}_1$ and $\mathbf{p}_2$ are the GCRS position vectors of CHIME and DSA-110, respectively, and $\mathbf{\hat{s}}$ is the unit vector pointing toward the source.
46	
47	\section{Results} \label{sec:results}
48	
49	We analyzed 12 co-detected bursts. For each event, we computed the "measured offset" ($\Delta \tau_{\text{obs}}$) as the difference between the frequency-corrected ToAs at both sites. The residual is then defined as:
50	\begin{equation}
51	    \mathcal{R} = \Delta \tau_{\text{obs}} - \tau_{\text{geo}}
52	\end{equation}
53	A residual of zero indicates perfect agreement between the observed timing and the theoretical prediction.
54	
55	\subsection{Residual Distribution}
56	
57	The residual distribution across our sample is shown in Figure \ref{fig:resid_burst}. We find a mean residual of $2.42$ ms with a standard deviation of $3.06$ ms. The median residual is $1.88$ ms. These results are consistent with the combined timing uncertainties of the two instruments, which are dominated by the coarse time resolution and pulse-width variations (FWHM).
58	
59	\begin{figure}[h!]
60	    \centering
61	    \includegraphics[width=\columnwidth]{toa_crossmatch_analysis_premium.png}
62	    \caption{TOA residual analysis. Panel A shows the residual (Measured - Geometric) for each burst, colored by DM. The green shaded region represents the median $1\sigma$ timing uncertainty ($\pm 2.5$ ms). Panel B shows the residual vs. DM systematics check.}
63	    \label{fig:resid_burst}
64	\end{figure}
65	
66	\section{Systematics Analysis} \label{sec:systematics}
67	
68	We performed a systematic correlation search (Figure \ref{fig:matrix}) between the observed residuals and several burst parameters to identify potential biases in our dispersion modeling or instrumental effects.
69	
70	\begin{figure*}[t]
71	    \centering
72	    \includegraphics[width=0.8\textwidth]{systematics_check_matrix.png}
73	    \caption{Systematic correlation search matrix. Residuals are plotted against DM, FWHM, Combined Uncertainty, and Time (MJD). Pearson correlation coefficients ($r$) and $p$-values are indicated. No correlations reach statistical significance ($p < 0.05$).}
74	    \label{fig:matrix}
75	\end{figure*}
76	
77	\subsection{Dispersion Measure Correlation}
78	
79	The correlation between residual and DM is negligible ($r=0.14, p=0.67$), suggesting that the $1/\nu^2$ scaling and the adopted $K_{\text{DM}}$ constant accurately describe the frequency-dependent delays across the observed DM range ($262 - 959 \, \text{pc cm}^{-3}$).
80	
81	\subsection{Timing Precision and FWHM}
82	
83	A moderate positive correlation exists between residuals and both burst FWHM ($r=0.48, p=0.11$) and combined measurement uncertainty ($r=0.49, p=0.11$). This is expected, as wider bursts have intrinsically poorer timing precision. However, neither reaches statistical significance ($p < 0.05$).
84	
85	\subsection{Temporal Stability}
86	
87	The correlation between residuals and time (MJD) yields $r=-0.54$ with $p=0.07$. While not formally significant, this suggestive trend indicates a possible drift in relative clock calibration or long-term baseline stability that warrants monitoring as the sample size increases.
88	
89	\section{Conclusions} \label{sec:conclusions}
90	
91	We have demonstrated high-precision ToA crossmatching between CHIME/FRB and DSA-110 for a sample of 12 co-detected bursts. The consistent residuals and lack of significant systematic correlations validate the current cross-calibration and dispersion delay models. Future co-detections will allow for more stringent tests of the cold-plasma dispersion law and finer monitoring of inter-observatory timing stability.
92	
93	\begin{acknowledgments}
94	This work utilized data from the CHIME/FRB collaboration and the Deep Synoptic Array (DSA-110).
95	\end{acknowledgments}
96	
97	\appendix
98	\section{Crossmatch Result Table}
99	
100	Table \ref{tab:results} summarizes the properties of the bursts included in this study. All residuals are calculated at a reference frequency of 400 MHz.
101	
102	\begin{table}[h!]
103	    \centering

105	    \begin{tabular}{ccccc}
106	    \hline \hline
107	    Nickname & DM (pc cm$^{-3}$) & MJD & FWHM (ms) & Residual (ms) \\ \hline
108	    Zach         & 262.37 & 59617.809 & 0.96 & 1.53 \\
109	    Whitney      & 462.17 & 59648.242 & 0.49 & 2.24 \\

info \\\"Provenance\\\"\\n\")\nmd.append(\"    Generated by `scratch/codetection/make_catalog_table.py` from the verified \"\n          \"pipeline (`normalize_codetection.py` → `validate_foreground.py` → \"\n          \"`ps1_strm_adjudicate.py` → `merge_final.py`). Source spreadsheet: \"\n          \"`DSA110_CHIME_Codetection_BurstProperties_Foreground`. Cosmology: Planck18.\\n\")\nwith open(os.path.join(REPO, \"docs-analysis\", \"foreground.md\"), \"w\") as fh:\n    fh.write(\"\\n\".join(md) + \"\\n\")\n\n# ---------- LaTeX deluxetable (manuscript) ----------\ntex = []\ntex.append(\"% Auto-generated by scratch/codetection/make_catalog_table.py — do not hand-edit.\")\ntex.append(\"\\\\startlongtable\")\ntex.append(\"\\\\begin{deluxetable*}{lllrrlllll}\")\ntex.append(\"\\\\tabletypesize{\\\\scriptsize}\")\ntex.append(\"\\\\tablecaption{Intervening foreground halos and clusters along the sightlines to \"\n           \"the 12 CHIME/DSA co-detected FRBs, validated against DESI Legacy DR9 (Zhou+2021 \"\n           \"photo-z), DESI DR1 spec-z, NED, and PS1-STRM. Verdicts: \\\\emph{confirmed} \"\n           \"(catalog $z<z_{\\\\rm host}$), \\\\emph{refuted} (background), \\\\emph{inconclusive} \"\n           \"($z$ within $1\\\\sigma$ of host, host $z$ unknown, or no trustworthy $z$). \"\n           \"\\\\label{tab:foreground}}\")\ntex.append(\"\\\\tablehead{\\\\colhead{Burst} & \\\\colhead{Type} & \\\\colhead{Obj ID} & \"\n           \"\\\\colhead{$b$} & \\\\colhead{$b/R_{500}$} & \\\\colhead{$z$} & \\\\colhead{$z$ src} & \"\n           \"\\\\colhead{Class} & \\\\colhead{Verdict} & \\\\colhead{Note}}\")\ntex.append(\"\\\\startdata\")\nprev = None\nfor _, r in cat.iterrows():\n    b = r.burst if r.burst != prev else \"\"\n    prev = r.burst\n    imp = \"\\\\nodata\" if pd.isna(r.impact_kpc) else f\"{r.impact_kpc:.0f}\"\n    br = \"\\\\nodata\" if pd.isna(r.b_over_r500) else f\"{r.b_over_r500:.2f}\"\n    note = str(r.reason).replace(\"σ\", \"$\\\\sigma$\").replace(\"→\", \"$\\\\to$\")\n    cls = str(r.classification).replace(\"_\", \"\\\\_\")\n    tex.append(f\"{b} & {r.type} & {r.obj_id} & {imp} & {br} & \"\n               f\"{zfmt(r.redshift, r.redshift_err, md=False)} & {r.redshift_source} & \"\n               f\"{cls} & {r.verdict} & {note} \\\\\\\\\")\ntex.append(\"\\\\enddata\")\ntex.append(\"\\\\tablecomments{All 49 candidates exist in $\\\\geq$1 public catalog. \"\n           \"$b$ is the proper impact parameter (kpc) at the object redshift; $b/R_{500}>1$ \"\n           \"(clusters) means the sightline passes outside the cluster. The original \"\n           \"spreadsheet photo-z column is unreliable for the PS1-STRM halos and is superseded \"\n           \"here by the catalog redshift.}\")\ntex.append(\"\\\\end{deluxetable*}\")\nwith open(os.path.join(REPO, \"foreground_table.tex\"), \"w\") as fh:\n    fh.write(\"\\n\".join(tex) + \"\\n\")\n\nprint(f\"wrote foreground_catalog.csv ({len(cat)} rows), docs-analysis/foreground.md, \"\n      f\"foreground_table.tex\")\nprint(f\"verdicts: confirmed={nconf} refuted={nref} inconclusive={ninc}\")\nprint(f\"md table data rows: {sum(1 for x in md if x.startswith('| ') and '---' not in x) - 1}\")\nprint(f\"tex data rows: {sum(1 for x in tex if x.endswith('\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\'))}\")\n"

# olcli — Overleaf CLI

**Command-line interface for Overleaf** — Sync, manage, and compile LaTeX projects from your terminal.

[![npm version](https://img.shields.io/npm/v/@aloth/olcli.svg)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@aloth/olcli)
[![AUR Package](https://img.shields.io/aur/version/olcli)](https://aur.archlinux.org/packages/olcli)
[![License: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/License-MIT-yellow.svg)](https://opensource.org/licenses/MIT)
[![AgentSkills](https://img.shields.io/badge/AgentSkills-compatible-blue)](https://agentskills.io)

Work with Overleaf projects directly from your command line. Edit locally with your favorite editor, version control with Git, and sync seamlessly with Overleaf's cloud compilation.

<p align="center">
  <img src="screenshots/demo.gif" alt="olcli demo" width="600">
</p>

## Features

**Full Overleaf command-line access:**

- 📋 **List** all your Overleaf projects
- ⬇️ **Pull** project files to local directory for offline editing
- ⬆️ **Push** local changes back to Overleaf
- 🔄 **Sync** bidirectionally with smart conflict detection
- 📄 **Compile** PDFs using Overleaf's remote compiler
- 📦 **Download** individual files or full project archives
- 📤 **Upload** files to projects
- 🗂️ **Preserve folder structure** when pushing nested files
- 🧹 **Skip generated `output.pdf`** during push/sync so compiled artifacts are not uploaded back to Overleaf
- ⚙️ **Support self-hosted Overleaf/ShareLaTeX instances** via configurable base URL and session cookie name
- 📊 **Output** compile artifacts (`.bbl`, `.log`, `.aux` for arXiv submissions)

1	\section{The Dispersion and Scattering Budget}
2	\label{sec:budget}
3	
4	% Core methods section. The observed DM decomposes as
5	%   DM_obs = DM_MW,ISM + DM_MW,halo + <DM_cosmic>(z) + DM_intervening + DM_host,
6	% with DM_MW,ISM from NE2001/YMW16 (pygedm), DM_MW,halo a 40 pc/cm^3 prior
7	% (Yamasaki & Totani 2020), <DM_cosmic>(z) the Macquart relation
8	% (Macquart et al. 2020; f_IGM=0.84, chi_e=0.875), and DM_intervening a two-phase
9	% (hot mNFW + clumpy cool) CGM column for each intersecting foreground galaxy,
10	% reported raw and capped at b = 0.1 R_vir (the galaxy-interior regime).
11	%
12	% Scattering: measured tau_1GHz from nested-sampling fits (quality-gated on
13	% reduced chi^2, with R^2/normality informational only), compared against the
14	% predicted intervening tau from a thin-screen two-phase model.
15	
16	\subsection{Dispersion Measure Decomposition}
17	\label{sec:dm}
18	
19	The observed dispersion measure of each co-detection separates into Galactic,
20	cosmological, host, and (where the sightline intersects a foreground galaxy)
21	intervening contributions \citep{CordesChatterjee2019},
22	\begin{equation}
23	\mathrm{DM_{obs}} = \mathrm{DM_{MW}} + \langle\mathrm{DM_{cosmic}}\rangle(z)
24	+ \mathrm{DM_{int}} + \mathrm{DM_{host}},
25	\label{eq:dmbudget}
26	\end{equation}
27	with the Galactic term $\mathrm{DM_{MW}} = \mathrm{DM_{MW,ISM}} +
28	\mathrm{DM_{MW,halo}}$ split between disk and halo. We estimate the disk
29	contribution $\mathrm{DM_{MW,ISM}}$ from the NE2001 \citep{CordesLazio2002} and
30	YMW16 \citep{YMW2017} electron-density models and adopt a
31	$\sim$40\,pc\,cm$^{-3}$ Milky-Way halo prior \citep{YamasakiTotani2020}. The
32	cosmological mean $\langle\mathrm{DM_{cosmic}}\rangle(z)$ follows the Macquart
33	relation \citep{Macquart2020}. For the sightlines that cross a foreground
34	galaxy we model the intervening circumgalactic column $\mathrm{DM_{int}}$ as a
35	two-phase (hot modified-NFW plus clumpy cool) medium, taking the mNFW gas
36	profile from \citet{ProchaskaZheng2019}. Such intervening halos can imprint
37	measurable dispersion and, where the gas is turbulent, scattering on FRB
38	sightlines \citep{Ocker2021}, although an individual quiescent halo may instead
39	yield only an upper limit on its scattering contribution \citep{Prochaska2019}.
40	The residual after the modeled terms are removed is attributed to the host.
41	
42	\subsection{Scattering Attribution}
43	\label{sec:scattering}
44	
45	We measure the pulse-broadening time and its frequency scaling from the
46	co-detected dynamic spectra and compare them against the scattering predicted
47	by each candidate screen: the Milky-Way ISM, an intervening circumgalactic
48	medium, or a host galaxy, where the host can dominate the scattering of a
49	heavily broadened burst \citep{Ocker2022}. The fits are produced by the
50	\texttt{dsa110-FLITS} pipeline (\texttt{pipeline/}).
51	
52	\subsubsection{The joint two-band fit}
53	\label{sec:jointfit}
54	
55	A single-band scattering fit cannot separate the scattering index $\alpha$ from
56	the scattering time, because the pulse broadening
57	$\tau(\nu)=\tau_{1\,\mathrm{GHz}}\,(\nu/1\,\mathrm{GHz})^{-\alpha}$ enters a
58	single band only through its value at that band's frequency: one band fixes the
59	product, not the slope. Co-detection breaks this degeneracy. We fit the
60	CHIME/FRB ($\sim$0.4--0.8\,GHz) and DSA-110 ($\sim$1.4\,GHz) dynamic spectra
61	\emph{simultaneously} with a shared sightline pair
62	$(\tau_{1\,\mathrm{GHz}},\alpha)$ and per-telescope pulse parameters (arrival
63	time $t_0$, intrinsic width $\zeta$, and a residual dispersion
64	$\delta\mathrm{DM}$). The $\sim$1\,GHz lever arm between the bands measures
65	$\alpha$ directly: the ratio of the two scattering times pins the slope, while
66	the shared normalization $\tau_{1\,\mathrm{GHz}}$ pins its value at 1\,GHz. With
67	$\alpha$ held at the Kolmogorov value $4.4$ \citep{Rickett1990}, the two bands
68	instead return $\tau_{1\,\mathrm{GHz}}$ estimates that disagree by up to an
69	order of magnitude for the same sightline---evidence that $\alpha\neq4.4$ along
70	these lines of sight.
71	
72	\subsubsection{Gain-marginalized likelihood}
73	\label{sec:gainmarg}
74	
75	The per-channel amplitude of an FRB spectrum is unknown and strongly modulated
76	by scintillation; carried as a free spectral envelope it leaves correlated
77	structure in the fit residuals and invalidates a $\chi^2$ goodness-of-fit test.
78	We therefore marginalize the per-channel gain analytically. With a Gaussian
79	prior on the gain the per-channel evidence is available in closed form (a
80	matched-filter likelihood), and the recovered gain absorbs both the burst
81	spectrum and the scintillation pattern. This removes the spectral and
82	scintillation structure from the residual, so that the reduced $\chi^2$ and the
83	lag-1 residual autocorrelation become meaningful quality gates, and it lowers
84	the sampled dimensionality. We
85	sample the posterior by nested sampling \citep{Skilling2004}, as implemented in
86	\texttt{dynesty} \citep{Speagle2020}, and quality-gate each fit on its reduced
87	$\chi^2$ and residual whiteness, treating $R^2$ and residual normality as
88	informational.
89	
90	\subsubsection{Multiple temporal components}
91	\label{sec:multicomp}
92	
93	Some bursts comprise more than one temporal sub-component, a common feature of
94	the resolved FRB population \citep{Hessels2019, Pleunis2021}. An unmodeled
95	second component is partially absorbed by a single scattered pulse---as a steeper slope
96	and a larger scattering time---and so biases the inferred $\alpha$. We extend
97	the likelihood to $N$ temporal components per band, each contributing its own
98	$(t_0,\zeta)$ while $(\tau_{1\,\mathrm{GHz}},\alpha)$ remain shared across both
99	bands and all components, and we select the number of components per band by
100	Bayesian evidence. Because the evidence normalization differs between likelihood
101	variants, the component counts are compared on a single matched grid in which
102	even the one-component model is evaluated through the multi-component
103	likelihood, so that evidence differences are meaningful. Component arrival times
104	within a band are ordered and separated by a data-derived minimum spacing,
105	keeping the fit identifiable at every prior sample. A clean single-component
106	co-detection in our sample, for which the joint fit returns
107	$\alpha=4.48\pm0.04$ with white residuals, validates the method; a
108	multi-component case is presented in Section~\ref{sec:results-alpha}.
109	% Validating clean case = burst internally labelled "freya" (swap to TNS name).
110

9	\subsection{Scattering index and burst multiplicity}
10	\label{sec:results-alpha}
11	
12	% Demonstrated multi-component case = burst internally labelled "zach"
13	% (swap to its TNS name). Numbers from the matched-normalization component grid.
14	A subset of our co-detected bursts is resolved into more than one temporal
15	component \citep{Pleunis2021}, and in these cases the inferred scattering index
16	depends on whether that multiplicity is modeled. We illustrate this with one co-detection whose
17	DSA-110 profile shows two sub-pulses while its CHIME/FRB profile presents a
18	single prominent peak yet fails the residual-whiteness gate. On the
19	matched-normalization grid, adding a second CHIME/FRB component is favored by
20	$\Delta\ln Z\approx+3.6\times10^{3}$ over the single-component model---roughly
21	forty times the evidence gain of adding a second DSA-110 component---and places
22	a broad companion $0.34$\,ms behind the main peak, blended beneath the
23	scattering tail where a simple peak search does not resolve it. Including this
24	component shifts the shared scattering index from $\alpha=3.32\pm0.01$ to
25	$\alpha=2.76\pm0.02$ and raises the scattering time from
26	$\tau_{1\,\mathrm{GHz}}=0.42$ to $0.56$\,ms. The second DSA-110 sub-pulse, which
27	a single-band fit leaves pinned at the minimum-separation prior bound, relocates
28	to its observed delay only once the CHIME/FRB component constrains the shared
29	$(\tau_{1\,\mathrm{GHz}},\alpha)$: the two bands are coupled through one
30	scattering law.
31

1	\section{Discussion}
2	\label{sec:discussion}
3	
4	% TODO: the coherent-picture cases — an intersecting foreground galaxy near the
5	% sightline midpoint with evidence for cool CGM gas, coincident with a heavily
6	% scattered burst, as an argument that an intervening galaxy is the scattering
7	% screen. Contrast with host- or Milky-Way-dominated sightlines where the
8	% predicted intervening tau falls far below the measurement.
9	
10	\subsection{Burst multiplicity as a systematic on the scattering index}
11	\label{sec:disc-alpha}
12	
13	The result of Section~\ref{sec:results-alpha} is a cautionary systematic for any
14	single-component scattering index. A temporal sub-component omitted from the
15	model is partially absorbed into the scattering tail, biasing $\alpha$ high: in
16	the case we examined the bias is $\Delta\alpha\approx0.56$, many times the formal
17	uncertainty. Because $\alpha$ is the quantity that distinguishes a Kolmogorov
18	turbulent screen ($\alpha\simeq4.4$; \citealp{Rickett1990}) from a shallower
19	spectrum, an unrecognized companion can masquerade as anomalous,
20	sub-Kolmogorov scattering---a regime in which measured pulse-broadening indices
21	already scatter well below the Kolmogorov value
22	\citep{Bhat2004}. We verified
23	that the favored second component is not an artifact of the likelihood:
24	reconstructing the single-component residual reproduces the whiteness statistic
25	that flagged the burst, the evidence gain is free of the eigenvalue-conditioning
26	pathology that a spurious near-degenerate component would trigger, and the
27	companion sits well inside the resolvable separation. Even the two-component
28	model, however, does not fully whiten the residual---a sharp rising edge
29	survives, consistent with an intrinsic fast rise, a limitation of the
30	scattered-pulse kernel, or a third component---so the corrected $\alpha$ should
31	be read as better-conditioned rather than final. A systematic re-fit of the
32	flagged co-detections in our sample is underway.
33
